newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH 96 BUDGET INCOME, OUTLAYS SEEN DOWN, GAP FLAT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH 96 BUDGET INCOME, OUTLAYS SEEN DOWN, GAP FLAT.

text.p: Poland's budget revenues are likely to be 1.7 percent smaller than planned this year with spending down 1.5 percent and the budget deficit flat at planned levels, the government said in its 1997 budget draft.

It said revenues were expected at 98.50 billion zlotys, 1.67 billion zlotys below target, because of smaller inflows from personal income taxes for 1995 and smaller than expected revenue from excise tax on spirits and tobacco products.

It also said income from the National Bank of Poland would be smaller than planned because of the large scale of costly open market operations through which the NBP offset the growth of the country's foreign currency reserves.
Budget spending is likely to be smaller than anticipated by 1.67 billion at 108.66 billion mainly due to lower costs of financing of Poland's foreign and domestic debt.

The costs of domestic debt servicing fell thanks to the higher share of the longest 52-week T-bills in sales, which shifted some of the costs to next year, as well as a faster than expected fall of T-bill yields.

Also spending on servicing interest and discount on bonds was smaller thanks to a lower than expected level of interest rates and the zloty's exchange rate and lower bond sales in general, the 1997 budget draft said.

Lower costs of foreign debt servicing came from favourable zloty cross rates, lower interest rates on international markets, lower payments to the World Bank due to the scrapping of some credit lines and lower payouts for government- guaranteed foreign credits.
The draft said the savings from lower budget spending would be used for unemployment benefits because the number of jobless was higher than expected.
